sets.t: Renal Anatomy and Physiology — Essay Questions

ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The kidneys are retroperitoneal beans that filter blood, regulate fluid balance, and produce hormones. Their anatomy determines how disease presents and guides clinical assessment.

b: Kidney size varies with age and body habitus
Cortex contains glomeruli; medulla houses loops of Henle

sections.p: The right kidney sits lower due to the liver; the left is higher and protected by the spleen. Internally, the renal hilum transmits vessels, nerves, and ureter.
b: Renal capsule provides protection but limits expansion
Renal sinus houses fat, vessels, and collecting system

sections.p: Anteriorly: adrenal gland, duodenum (right), pancreas (left). Posteriorly: quadratus lumborum, psoas. These relationships affect spread of infection or trauma.
b: Retroperitoneal location means peritoneal signs are absent in renal bleed

sections.p: Renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta at L1‑L2; segmental branches supply cortex and medulla. Venous drainage follows the same pattern into the IVC.

t.b: Is there arterial stenosis or thrombosis?

sections.p: Sympathetic fibers from T10‑L2 travel with renal vessels; parasympathetic input is minimal. Pain is referred to the flank and groin via T10‑L1 dermatomes.
b: Kidney colic follows the same pathway as ureteric pain

sections.p: Nephrons filter ~180 L/day; reabsorption and secretion fine‑tune electrolytes, acid‑base, and volume. The juxtaglomerular apparatus releases renin, linking anatomy to blood pressure control.
b: Cortical nephrons handle most filtration; medullary nephrons concentrate urine

sections.p: Obstruction, infection, trauma, and vascular disease all relate to anatomy. For example, a stone lodged at the ureteropelvic junction causes flank pain and hydronephrosis.
Palpate for flank tenderness, percuss for dullness, and auscultate for bruits over the renal arteries. Recognize that a palpable kidney often signals chronic disease.
b: A bruit suggests renal artery stenosis, common in hypertension

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe flank pain with vomiting (possible renal colic or infarction)

faq.q: Why is the right kidney lower than the left?
faq.a: The liver occupies space on the right, pushing the kidney down.

faq.q: What does a renal bruit indicate?
faq.a: Turbulent flow from renal artery stenosis, a treatable cause of hypertension.

faq.q: How does kidney size help diagnose disease?
faq.a: Enlarged kidneys suggest acute inflammation or obstruction; small kidneys point to chronic scarring.

exam: Describe the relationship between the renal hilum structures and how this influences surgical approach.
Explain why flank pain from a renal stone radiates to the groin.
List the imaging modalities for suspected renal artery stenosis and their diagnostic criteria.
